prior_source: docs/research/merchant-feature-benchmark-2026-11-16.md (sections: Foundation priorities B01-B12; Merchant workflow priorities B13-B24; Advanced capabilities B25-B32). The prior document's BTCPay, Bitcart, LNbits, SatSale, ZEUS, Alby, Phoenixd, Breez, OpenNode, CoinGate, and Strike comparison remains historical secondary-competitor context; current_claim_ids reference only the 2026-11-17 vendor and bitcoin-native bundles.

items.title: Canonical invoice and payment lifecycle
items.carried_forward_requirement: Keep order, payment attempts, received funds, confirmation policy, refunds, and fulfillment as distinct states, with explicit handling for partial, late, excess, expiry, reorganization, cancellation, and refund outcomes.
items.remaining_research: Current sources document examples of invoice and tender states, but do not establish a shared OpenBMT commerce lifecycle or end-to-end state transition acceptance criteria across Bitcoin, cash, and optional card.

items.title: Versioned local payment interface
items.carried_forward_requirement: Provide a documented versioned local contract to create/query invoices and correlate orders; HTTP hosting remains an optional adapter, not a default merchant-server requirement.
items.remaining_research: Competitor API documentation is available, but the local OpenBMT API contract, versioning, permissions, stability, and app integration behavior remain to be specified and validated.

items.title: Durable local payment events
items.carried_forward_requirement: Persist local payment-state events with the corresponding sale state and recover them after interruption; treat an optional outbound webhook as a separate adapter.
items.remaining_research: The current claims cover vendor callback/webhook behavior and some pending-payment visibility, not the local durable journal/event contract or atomic state coupling required by the benchmark.

items.title: Query and reconciliation
items.carried_forward_requirement: Allow recovery from missed events, restart, or ambiguous payment attempts by querying current state and reconciling without charging or fulfilling twice.
items.remaining_research: Research vendor reconciliation patterns and exceptions, then define OpenBMT idempotency, local/remote query cursor, unknown-outcome repair, and interruption acceptance tests.

items.title: Immutable order and quote references
items.carried_forward_requirement: Retain the exact amount, currency, exchange-rate terms, expiry, order reference, and order revision associated with each payment request.
items.remaining_research: Current records show invoice/request references and URI requirements but do not establish a versioned immutable OpenBMT quote/order-reference contract or its revision and expiry behavior.

items.title: Customer recovery for payment exceptions
items.carried_forward_requirement: Explain remaining balances, overpayments, late payments, expiry, and invalidated receipts to customers and staff, and provide a clearly authorized next action.
items.remaining_research: Document exception-specific customer and staff recovery actions, including whether to pay remainder, refund, reissue, hold, or manually resolve; verify behavior across all tender types.

items.title: Refund claim and payout tracking
items.carried_forward_requirement: Let the customer provide a refund destination, then require merchant review, explicit approval, signing, broadcast, and payout tracking as separate steps.
items.remaining_research: Vendor refund behaviors are documented, but a general Bitcoin refund-claim link, destination validation, approval authority, signature boundary, payout status, and replay-safe workflow still require product research and acceptance criteria.

items.title: Scoped users and integration credentials
items.carried_forward_requirement: Separate cashier, manager, owner, invoice creation, reporting, refund request, and spending permissions; make integration credentials independently scoped, revocable, and auditable.
items.remaining_research: Compare current documented role and API scopes, then define OpenBMT actor/resource/action boundaries, credential lifecycle, device screens, and explicit spending authority; competitor permissions do not establish a native implementation.

items.title: Searchable payment history and audit trail
items.carried_forward_requirement: Search a sale by order/reference, inspect its state changes, and identify who authorized a sensitive action.
items.remaining_research: Current documentation covers invoice/history search and selected action attribution, but a cross-tender OpenBMT audit trail with actor, approval, event history, and recovery links remains to be specified.

items.title: Reconciliation and accounting exports
items.carried_forward_requirement: Export gross receipts, actual fees, refunds, payment method, timestamps, and fiat reference values for local accounting without requiring a cloud ledger.
items.remaining_research: Vendor reporting/export examples do not establish a complete local multi-tender accounting report; define fields, privacy limits, exact satoshi values, fee provenance, and reconciliation tests.

items.title: Hot start and independently controlled savings
items.carried_forward_requirement: Explain cold-wallet pairing and authority choices, retain a dependable receiving path, and keep savings keys out of checkout; make merchant control and recovery understandable.
items.remaining_research: Wallet custody and watch-only alternatives are documented in competitor/native requirements, but validate OpenBMT setup, key authority, ordinary wallet compatibility, recovery, and receive-to-savings merchant flows.

items.title: Recoverable backups and restore checks
items.carried_forward_requirement: State clearly what a backup restores and demonstrate device/service recovery with ordinary dependencies unavailable, including Lightning channel-state limitations.
items.remaining_research: Competitor backup and native recovery requirements are captured; OpenBMT restore tests, kit printing, device drills, Lightning state recovery, and backup boundary explanations remain necessary.

items.title: Keypad, cart, and local catalog
items.carried_forward_requirement: Support amount-only and item-based checkout without duplicate entry, with a configurable local catalog, variations/modifiers, basket management, and production-safe item handling.
items.remaining_research: Current sources document competitor catalog, modifier, barcode and POS behaviors, but do not establish OpenBMT catalog CRUD, keypad/cart workflows, modifier pricing, or merchant validation. Preserve the modifier requirement despite platform-specific implementation differences.

items.title: Tax, discounts, and tips
items.carried_forward_requirement: Preserve merchant-configured tax, discount, and tip behavior in price snapshots and provide pricing tools without presenting the product as tax advice.
items.remaining_research: Current docs capture multiple vendor-specific tax/discount/tip behaviors; OpenBMT tax jurisdiction rules, precedence, exact calculation/snapshot, rounding, tip rules, and Bitcoin price treatment need separate decisions and tests.

items.title: Inventory and stock events
items.carried_forward_requirement: Reserve or decrement stock once at a defined sale outcome, then reconcile cancellations, returns, partial/late payments, and receipt interruptions without double adjustment.
items.remaining_research: Current vendor docs cover inventory adjustments/counts/transfers and some stock-on-sale behavior; OpenBMT reservation timing, tender independence, idempotent decrement, cancellation/refund reversal, and cross-location event rules remain unvalidated.

items.title: Complete one commerce integration
items.carried_forward_requirement: Complete one end-to-end commerce integration across order creation, payment, and fulfillment, then reuse the contract for other platforms.
items.remaining_research: Research includes platform-specific capabilities and APIs but does not establish one tested OpenBMT integration from order creation through payment and fulfillment; preserve WooCommerce/prototype assessment and native-provider candidate review.

items.title: Receipts and customer status pages
items.carried_forward_requirement: Show amount, method, state, reference, and refund progress; support local print/export and make external delivery opt-in.
items.remaining_research: Vendor receipt behavior is documented, but OpenBMT receipt projection, privacy-limited fields, actual printer/email delivery, offline behavior, and customer-visible payment/refund status page remain to validate.

items.title: Long-lived invoices and installments
items.carried_forward_requirement: Share a request with a due date, track multiple payments/installments with fresh payment attempts, and preserve customer-paid renewal as the default model.
items.remaining_research: BTCPay requests/subscriptions and native partial/late payment needs are documented, but OpenBMT API/UI integration, request expiry, installment accounting, reminders, and no-auto-debit renewal experience remain to specify.

items.title: Payment buttons and minimal forms
items.carried_forward_requirement: Offer embeddable payments, donations, and campaigns without requiring payer accounts or collecting unnecessary identity data.
items.remaining_research: Shareable requests and URI handoff are evidenced, but reusable public button/form surfaces, payer data minimization, public payment status, and integration boundaries require product research.

items.title: Multiple registers and locations
items.carried_forward_requirement: Make per-register authority, payment references, inventory effects, and reports intelligible across locations.
items.remaining_research: Current vendor evidence covers location configuration and reporting examples, but OpenBMT device/register separation, cross-location permissions, ledger references, offline reconciliation, and multi-location administration remain unverified.

items.title: Store and tenant isolation
items.carried_forward_requirement: For any multi-merchant installation, isolate each merchant's wallets, credentials, records, and backups.
items.remaining_research: Current evidence covers competitor store contexts and API scopes; OpenBMT tenant boundaries, wallet ownership, data separation, backup/restore isolation, and administrator threat model remain to research. This mapping does not approve a shared hosted deployment.

items.title: Receiving and settlement health
items.carried_forward_requirement: Explain receiving availability, stale observations, pending transfers, fee budget, liquidity, and output-maintenance needs in plain language; never represent a point-in-time observation as a route guarantee.
items.remaining_research: Native liquidity/availability requirements and competitor operations are documented, but a unified merchant controller, surfaced health state, timing, fee and capacity estimates, and recovery UI remain research/validation work.

items.title: Optional webhooks and owner notifications
items.carried_forward_requirement: Send signed, owner-configured outbound events to an existing merchant receiver while keeping local checkout independent; include stable identities, bounded retries, manual replay, query reconciliation, payload minimization, explicit availability limits, and no wallet-spending authority.
items.remaining_research: Current corpus documents selected competitor callbacks, signatures, retries, and state events. OpenBMT local event and optional webhook contract, contact/data inventory, retry/outbox behavior, recipient controls, and failure-boundary tests remain unresearched; no merchant web server or company relay is implied.

items.title: Developer test mode and operating diagnostics
items.carried_forward_requirement: Provide regtest fixtures, API examples, event replay, redacted local logs, and a test path that does not move real funds.
items.remaining_research: Current vendor docs include sandbox, diagnostics, and recovery patterns; package and validate the OpenBMT developer journey, regtest fixtures, local replay, log redaction, and failure simulations.

items.title: Payjoin
items.carried_forward_requirement: Research optional Payjoin support as a way to reduce separate on-chain consolidation work while preserving ordinary-address checkout and requiring payer wallet cooperation.
items.remaining_research: No current vendor or native bundle claim establishes Payjoin support or compatibility. Retain as P2 research; assess wallet support, protocol versions, receiver requirements, privacy, failure fallback, and merchant proof before roadmap commitment.

items.title: Reusable offers and payment names
items.carried_forward_requirement: Research BOLT12 and LNURL reusable offers/payment names for recurring tips and donations, while preserving sale-specific amount/quote references and explicit endpoint/network assumptions.
items.remaining_research: Native bundle covers payment URI/QR, NFC handoff, Lightning invoice interop, and URI safety, but not BOLT12/LNURL offer interoperability, address/DNS infrastructure, reusable offer expiry, or cross-wallet tests.

items.title: Scoped NWC connections
items.carried_forward_requirement: Research Nostr Wallet Connect as an optional connection to an existing wallet/node with separate invoice, read, and explicitly granted spending capabilities, expiry, revocation, and activity review.
items.remaining_research: Current API role/credential claims are not NWC evidence. Retain separate protocol research for NWC permissions, budgets, relay/service dependencies, revocation, wallet compatibility, key authority, and spend authorization UX.

items.title: Recurring invoices and reminders
items.carried_forward_requirement: Support renewable memberships/services through customer-paid renewals or explicitly authorized payer-side automation; model reminders, grace periods, and prepaid-credit liability separately.
items.remaining_research: Current docs show vendor subscription/request functions, but preserve OpenBMT's customer-paid renewal preference, no universal arbitrary-wallet auto-debit promise, credit liability assessment, and renewal recovery rules.

items.title: Digital goods and access fulfillment
items.carried_forward_requirement: Deliver digital goods or access once after a defined payment state, record acknowledgment, and recover safely after interruption without duplicate fulfillment.
items.remaining_research: No current vendor/native bundle claim in this corpus establishes digital delivery or access control; retain as a separate workflow for primary-source research and end-to-end validation.

items.title: Authorized batch payouts
items.carried_forward_requirement: Explore batching approved refunds or supplier payments when economical, with explicit merchant approval, destination review, fee authority, UTXO reservation, external signing, and payout tracking; do not imply generalized automated supplier spending.
items.remaining_research: Current claims cover refund claims, PSBT signing, fee/UTXO authority requirements, but not an OpenBMT batch payout workflow, accounting, policy, authorization thresholds, or collision/recovery behavior.

items.title: Extension and adapter contract
items.carried_forward_requirement: Permit commerce extensions and platform adapters without loading untrusted code into wallet-key authority or silently broadening permissions; keep interfaces reviewable and revocable.
items.remaining_research: Current docs include competitor plugins, app extensions, and integration boundaries, but OpenBMT's process isolation, extension signature/trust, permission model, update lifecycle, and adapter contract remain unresearched.

items.title: NFC and payment handoff compatibility
items.carried_forward_requirement: Transport the same amount-bound request through tested NFC, QR, copy, and deep-link paths, then publish a device and wallet compatibility matrix.
items.remaining_research: Native bundle explicitly retains NFC URI handoff and Lightning QR interoperability; card tap-to-pay claims describe card acceptance, not Bitcoin NFC handoff. Physical-wallet tests, amount binding, fallback, and broader compatibility matrix remain outstanding.
